He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Love attended [[Christian Brothers College High School]] in [[St. Louis|St. Louis, Missouri]], and was coached by [[Justin Tatum]], father of NBA player [[Jayson Tatum]]. He averaged 18.9 points and 4.3 rebounds per game as a junior as he transitioned to point guard.{{cite news |last1=Dopirak |first1=Dustin |title=For Caleb Love, transitioning to point guard means becoming the 'alpha male' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/974270/2019/05/14/for-caleb-love-transitioning-to-point-guard-means-becoming-the-alpha-male/ |access-date=April 19, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=May 14, 2019}} He led the school to the Class 5 runner-up to [[Rock Bridge High School]]. Love scored a career-high 42 points against [[East St. Louis High School]] as a senior and also scored 40 points against [[Cardinal Ritter High School]].{{cite news |last1=Kvidahl |first1=David |title=All-Metro boys basketball player of the year: Love's prestigious CBC career cut short by coronavirus pandemic |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/all-metro/boys-basketball/all-metro-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-loves-prestigious-cbc-career-cut-short-by/article_cbddb486-705f-11ea-921e-fb63413acfd6.html |accessdate=April 19, 2020 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=March 29, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 26.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 2.6 steals per game and led the team to the Class 5 Final Four. Love was named [[Mr. Show-Me Basketball]] and Gatorade Player of the Year in Missouri.{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Corey |title=CBC's Caleb Love named Mr. Show-Me Basketball and Gatorade Player of the Year in Missouri |url=https://www.ksdk.com/article/sports/cbcs-caleb-love-named-mr-show-me-basketball-and-gatorade-player-of-the-year-in-missouri/63-2f987901-46ac-440b-a7ad-97c8d2eb9204 |accessdate=April 19, 2020 |work=KSDK |date=March 26, 2020}} He was named [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]], becoming the second player from Christian Brothers to be so honored after [[Larry Hughes]] in 1997.{{cite news |last1=Kvidahl |first1=David |title=CBC's Love named to McDonald's All-American team |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/cbc-s-love-named-to-mcdonald-s-all-american-team/article_f84b65c2-3e55-11ea-84d2-2b30adafc7db.html |accessdate=April 19, 2020 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=January 24, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Love was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2020 class, according to major recruiting services. He committed to playing college basketball for [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] on October 1, 2019, choosing the Tar Heels over [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], among others.{{cite magazine |last1=Wilkerson-New |first1=Brant |title=2020 PG Caleb Love commits to Carolina |url=https://www.si.com/college/unc/basketball/caleb-love-commits-to-unc |accessdate=April 19, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 1, 2019}} Love was attracted to North Carolina because of coach [[Roy Williams (basketball coach)|Roy Williams]] and the opportunity to play lead guard.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=College basketball scorers with 17 points and posted four assists and two steals in a 79–60 win over the [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]].{{cite news |last1=Palermo |first1=Gregg |title=CBC grad Caleb Love leads all scorers in North Carolina debut |url=https://fox2now.com/sports/cbc-grad-caleb-love-leads-all-scorers-in-north-carolina-debut/ |access-date=November 26, 2020 91–87|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=February 7, 2021}} On February 8, 2021, Love earned his second [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) Freshman of the week honor.{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2021/2/8/athlete-awards-uvas-hauser-uncs-love-claim-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=UVA's Hsuser, UNC's Love Claim Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|date=February 8, 2021 |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=February 8, 2021}} He was named to the ACC All-Freshman Team after averaging 10.5 points and 3.5 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=McMillan |first1=Sherrell |title=Caleb Love Returning to UNC |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Caleb-Love-UNC-Basketball-Returning-Freshman-Point-Guard-162959497/ |access-date=July 6, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=March 26, 2021}} Following the season, longtime Tar Heel head coach [[Roy Williams (basketball coach)|Roy Williams]] retired. After deliberating, Love decided to return to [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina|Chapel Hill]] for his sophomore season. ====Sophomore==== In head coach [[Hubert Davis]]' first season in charge after the retirement of Williams, Love was a key piece of a starting lineup that became known as the "Iron Five." The lineup included himself, [[R. J. Davis]], [[Leaky Black]], Oklahoma transfer [[Brady Manek]], and [[Armando Bacot]]. In what began as an up-and-down season for both Love and the rest of the team, the "Iron Five" became crucial to the team's success down the stretch in their run to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship game]]. In total on the season, Love set career highs in three point field goal percentage, games played, and starts, starting all but one of the 39 games played that season. He averaged 15.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game on the season, averaging 37.1% from the floor and 36% from beyond the three-point line. In the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], Love scored 27 of his then career-high 30 points in the second half of a 73–66 win over fourth-seeded [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in the Sweet Sixteen.{{cite news|first=Eddie|last=Pells|title=If the shoe fits: Love leads Carolina over UCLA into Elite 8|date=March 25, 2022|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-north-carolina-tar-heels-mens-basketball-st-peters-peacocks-mens-basketball-ucla-bruins-mens-basketball-sports-2a42c4860b70e73463551d9840189bc2|access-date=March 26, 2022}} In the following [[Final Four]] matchup with the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], Love scored 28 points, including a late three-point shot seen as pivotal in the Tar Heels' 81–77 victory.{{cite web |title=Caleb Love drops 28 as UNC takes down Duke in Final Four {{!}} NCAA.com |url=https://www.ncaa.com/video/basketball-men/2022-04-02/caleb-love-drops-28-unc-takes-down-duke-final-four |website=NCAA.com |access-date=April 3, 2022 |language=en}}{{cite web |last1=Pearson |first1=Zack |title=Caleb Love's late three pointer helps lift UNC past Duke |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/watch-caleb-love-three-pointer-033839998.html |website=Yahoo! Sports |date=April 3, 2022 |access-date=April 3, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=UNC hangs on, closes Coach K's career in classic |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33658635/north-carolina-tar-heels-advance-men-basketball-national-final-close-duke-blue-devils-coach-mike-krzyzewski-career |website=ESPN |access-date=April 3, 2022 |language=en |date=April 3, 2022}} In the Finals, he rolled his ankle and was shooting poorly, but still had a chance to tie the game despite [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] coming back in the second half.{{Cite web |last=Thamel |first=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |date=April 5, 2022 |title=Injuries, vomit, shaky floorboards and a painful loss: The cascading calamities of North Carolina's second half |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33673139/north-carolina-men-basketball-terrible-horrible-no-good-very-bad-half |access-date=April 6, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He air-balled a closely guarded step-back three-pointer, and UNC lost the title. He finished the game with 13 points on 5-of-24 shooting.{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Grant |date=April 6, 2022 |title=Expert Analysis: Dealing With Defeat, Tar Heel Toughness, Puff Johnson |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/LongFormArticle/Sherrell-McMillan-UNC-Kansas-National-Championship-Expert-Perspective-Dealing-With-Defeat-Tar-Heel-Toughness-Puff-Johnson-185777633/ |access-date=April 6, 2022 |website=InsideCarolina.com |language=en-US}} ====Junior==== After the late-season success of the prior season, Love, Black, Davis, and Bacot all decided to return for the 2022–23 season. Despite a pre-season No.1 ranking and massive expectations, the season went awry quickly for Love and his teammates. Still, Love was a key piece of the starting lineup and started 32 of the 33 games the team played (his lone appearance off the bench came on UNC's senior night, where tradition dictates that the starting lineup consists of all seniors on the team). The Tar Heels stumbled to a 20–13 record in Hubert Davis's second season. Love, despite shooting worse from the foul line and three-point line in his junior season, set new career highs in overall field-goal percentage (37.8%), points per game (16.7), and rebounds per game (3.7).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/4433144/caleb-love|title=Caleb Love Stats|website=ESPN.com|publisher=ESPN|access-date=March 20, 2023}} Following the season, Love entered the transfer portal, announcing his intentions to play elsewhere in his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Caleb-Love-Leaving-UNC-Basketball-Transfer-Portal-206365059/|title=BREAKING: Caleb Love Leaving UNC, Entering Transfer Portal|last=Smith|first=Adam|website=InsideCarolina.com|publisher=247 Sports|date=March 27, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} ===Arizona=== ====Senior==== After much speculation, Love originally committed to play his senior season at [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/36105322/former-north-carolina-guard-caleb-love-transferring-michigan|title=Former North Carolina guard Caleb Love transferring to Michigan|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|website=ESPN.com|publisher=ESPN|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} However, just over a month after committing to Michigan, Love decommitted from the Wolverines and headed back into transfer portal, reportedly due to an issue with transfer credits.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10076447-report-caleb-love-wont-transfer-to-michigan-unc-return-not-on-the-table|title=Report: Caleb Love Won't Transfer to Michigan; UNC Return Not on the Table|last=Rapp|first=Timothy|website=bleacherreport.com|publisher=Bleacherreport|date=May 17, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2023}} He announced his commitment to the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] via social media on May 30, 2023.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10077192-former-unc-star-caleb-love-transfers-to-arizona-after-decommitting-from-michigan|title=Former UNC Star Caleb Love Transfers to Arizona After Decommitting from Michigan|last=Walsh|first=Erin|website=bleacherreport.com|publisher=Bleacher Report|date=May 30, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2023}} Love made his Wildcat debut on November 6, 2023, scoring 12 points and dishing out four assists in a 122–59 victory over [[Morgan State Bears basketball|Morgan State]].{{cite web |last1=Marshall |first1=John |title=Boswell scores 18, No. 12 Arizona dominates Morgan State 122-59 in season opener |url=https://apnews.com/article/arizona-morgan-state-tommy-lloyd-caleb-love-4863c3d4ab8871a1d21a21e7e5b2d8f0 |website=AP |date=November 7, 2023 |access-date=March 2, 2024}} Love made his return to [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] on November 10 and beat No. 2 Duke 78–73, snapping their 17-game home winning streak.{{cite web |title=No. 12 Arizona basketball snaps No. 2 Duke's home winning streak with full team effort |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3537929/arizona-beats-duke-snap-winning-streak/ |website=arizonasports.com |date=November 11, 2023 |access-date=March 2, 2024}} On December 16, Love had a game-high 29 points and six rebounds in a 92–84 loss to No. 3 [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], marking Arizona's first loss of the season.{{cite web |title=Loyer, Smith Lead No. 3 Purdue Past No. 1 Arizona 92-84 in NCAA Showdown |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2023/12/16/mens-basketball-loyer-smith-lead-no-3-purdue-past-no-1-arizona-92-84-in-ncaa-showdown.aspx |website=arizonawildcats.com |date=December 16, 2023 |access-date=March 2, 2024}} On January 6 against [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]], Love had 23 points, six rebounds, and six assists on 60% from the field in a 92–73 victory.{{cite web |last1=Marshall |first1=John |title=Love scores 15 of his 23 points during decisive stretch in No. 10 Arizona's 92-73 win over Utah |url=https://apnews.com/article/arizona-utah-score-76aff7846adf05e982fe13e0f0358236 |website=AP |date=January 7, 2024 |access-date=March 2, 2024}} The next game against [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], Love finished with 28 points and eight rebounds in a tight 73–70 road loss.{{cite web |last1=Guzeloglu |first1=Melisa |title=No. 8 Arizona MBB falls short against Washington State |url=https://wildcat.arizona.edu/152460/sports/s-mbb-wsu-recap-24/ |website=The Daily Wildcat |access-date=March 2, 2024}} On January 27, Love went 12-for-18 from the field and scored a career-high 36 points in a 87–78 road victory against [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]. His 36 points tied the single-game scoring record at [[Matthew Knight Arena]].{{cite web |title=Caleb Love Scores a Career-High 36 Points as No. 9 Arizona Beats Oregon 87-78 |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2024/1/27/mens-basketball-caleb-love-scores-a-career-high-36-points-as-no-9-arizona-beats-oregon-87-78.aspx |website=arizonawildcats.com |date=January 27, 2024 |access-date=March 2, 2024}} On February 8, Love recorded his first career double-double in a triple overtime road victory against Utah, finishing with 19 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite web |title=Caleb Love records first career double-double; Dunn starting for PSU; Big games for Styles, Adams |url=https://www.tarheeltimes.com/article148966.aspx |website=Tar Heel Times |access-date=March 2, 2024}} Against [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] on February 24, Love poured in 28 points and reached 2,000 collegiate points in a 91–75 win.{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Caleb Love nets 2000th career point, leads Arizona over Washington |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2024/02/24/caleb-love-nets-2000th-career-point-leads-arizona-over-washington/72731010007/ |website=AZCentral |access-date=March 2, 2024}} On March 12, 2024, Love was awarded the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year Award]] and became the tenth Arizona Wildcat to win the award. Love averaged a team-high 18.7 points on 43% from the field and 35.2% from three-point range. He added 4.9 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 1.2 steals in 32.2 minutes played.{{cite web |title=Arizona Wildcats' Caleb Love named 2023-24 Pac-12 Player of the Year |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3544318/arizona-wildcats-caleb-love-named-2023-24-pac-12-player-of-the-year/ |website=Arizona Sports |date=March 12, 2024 |access-date=March 12, 2024}} He helped Arizona earn the No. 2 seed in the West region of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA Tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Mendoza |first1=Jordan |title=What to know about Caleb Love, the North Carolina transfer who is now leading Arizona |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/pac12/2024/03/18/arizona-caleb-love-march-madness/73011879007/ |website=USA Today |access-date=March 18, 2024}} They advanced to the Sweet 16, where they lost to No. 6 [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] 77–72, with Love missing all nine of his three-point attempts.{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Ryan |title=March Madness: Clemson shuts down Caleb Love, Arizona to reach first Elite Eight since 1980 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/march-madness-clemson-shuts-down-caleb-love-arizona-to-reach-first-elite-eight-since-1980-012218066.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=March 28, 2024}} ====Graduate==== Love announced via his social media accounts on May 29, 2024, that he would withdraw from the [[2024 NBA Draft]] and return to Arizona for his graduate season. He averaged 17.2 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite news |last1=Cowley |first1=Jared |title=Blazers to sign Arizona guard Caleb Love to two-way contract: Report |url=https://www.kgw.com/article/sports/nba/blazers/blazers-arizona-guard-caleb-love/283-afef47a1-8dfe-4322-a8a2-cc18269edee9 |access-date=June 30, 2025 |work=KGW |date=June 26, 2025}} ==Professional career== On July 1, 2025, after going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA Draft]], Love signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Caleb Love to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-caleb-love-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2025|access-date=July 12, 2025}} On November 21, against the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]], Love scored a career high of 26 points, and tallied seven rebounds, five assists, and one steal in 38 minutes of action off the bench.{{Cite web |last=Kunz |first=Reese |title=Caleb Love is doing something nobody expected to save the Blazers offense |url=https://ripcityproject.com/caleb-love-doing-nobody-expected-save-blazers-offense |website=Rip City Project |access-date=November 22, 2025 |language=en }} On July 5, 2026, Love signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN CALEB LOVE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT {{!}} Philadelphia Sixers
